Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage is overwhelmingly dominated by Anthropic's IPO filing, with every major outlet dissecting its eye-popping $80.7 billion first-half loss, $16.3 billion revenue, and unusual governance structure ahead of a potential record-breaking Nasdaq debut. Secondary focus is on macro and markets: the Fed's rate decision, a fiscal reckoning for Brazil after Lula's surprise re-election rattled investors, Beijing's intervention to stem a stock rout, and a mixed Q3 corporate earnings season.

stories.headline: Anthropic Files for IPO in Global Race to Raise Cash for AI
stories.summary: Anthropic's S-1 filing revealed $16.3 billion in first-half revenue alongside an $80.7 billion net loss (mostly an accounting charge), a five-class share structure giving founders permanent 50.1% voting control, and plans to list on Nasdaq as "ANT" as soon as Thanksgiving week at a valuation reportedly targeted between $1.5 and $2 trillion.

stories.headline: The Fed Is Expected to Hold Rates Steady. Warsh Will Have to Explain Why.
stories.summary: The Fed is expected to keep rates unchanged at its meeting this week even though inflation is reportedly moving in the wrong direction, putting pressure on Chair Kevin Warsh to justify the decision; markets are also watching for cues ahead of the decision.

stories.headline: Lula Faces a Fiscal Reckoning After Brazil's Market Rout
stories.summary: Brazil's currency suffered its worst day in more than 25 years as investors grew alarmed about economic management following Lula's upset re-election, though at least one prominent investor is betting the sell-off is overdone and preparing to buy.

stories.headline: China Steps In to Rescue Stocks, But the Market Continues to Fall
stories.summary: Beijing deployed its "national team" of state-owned investment funds to stem a stock market rout, but investors are reportedly unsure the intervention will succeed this time.

stories.headline: UPS, Coca-Cola and JetBlue Earnings Offer Upbeat Notes
stories.summary: UPS beat Wall Street expectations and raised full-year guidance for a second straight quarter, Coca-Cola lifted its 2026 outlook despite soft North America volumes, and JetBlue shares jumped after the airline pledged a return to profitability next year.

stories.headline: Whirlpool Cuts Outlook Again on Muted Demand, Soaring Costs
stories.summary: Whirlpool slashed its full-year guidance for the third time in 2026 and is now forecasting its first annual loss in decades, blaming weak consumer demand and elevated commodity costs.

stories.headline: A $300 Billion 'Debt Wall' Is Looming Over Private-Equity Backed Companies
stories.summary: WSJ reports that roughly $300 billion in risky corporate loans tied to private-equity backed firms come due in 2028 and 2029, with software companies accounting for about a third of that exposure.

stories.headline: FTC and 20 States Sue Dollar General, Alleging Retailer Overcharged Shoppers
stories.summary: The FTC and attorneys general from 20 states filed suit against Dollar General, alleging the discount retailer systematically charged customers more than its advertised prices.

Business.gaps: No recent business-relevant items were found for Puck or Business Insider in this window.

US politics.overview: US political coverage over the past 24-48 hours is dominated by the final week before the November 3 midterms, with new polling showing a Democratic advantage, Cook Political Report further tilting House ratings toward Democrats, and the Trump DOJ's aggressive late-cycle interventions in election disputes. Congress-focused outlets are also tracking a crowded lame-duck legislative agenda (NDAA, FISA, funding/debt limit) and intraparty GOP anxiety about the midterm map, while Melania Trump's Ukraine ceasefire and Trump's tariff politics also feature prominently.

stories.headline: New NPR/PBS/Marist poll shows Democrats holding an edge a week before midterms
stories.summary: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds Democrats retain a significant lead heading into Election Day, though lagging enthusiasm among some key groups raises questions about how large their gains will be. The Hill separately reported the same survey found Democrats with an 8-point advantage nationally.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report shifts House ratings further toward Democrats
stories.summary: Cook Political Report's latest ratings update moved 19 more House seats toward Democrats, putting the party favored outright in the 218 seats needed for a majority and projecting a likely gain of 12 to 22 seats. The Washington Post and The Hill both reported the shift could produce bigger Democratic majorities than the 2006 or 2018 wave years.

stories.headline: Trump's DOJ escalates election-related interventions in final midterm stretch
stories.summary: With days left before the midterms, the Justice Department is pursuing a preemptive lawsuit to potentially delay certification of Alaska's Senate race if Democrat Mary Peltola wins, alongside a separate suit seeking to block roughly 20,000 suspected noncitizen ballots in California. The Hill reported Peltola's campaign has asked a judge to dismiss the Alaska suit, while NPR noted congressional Democrats are forming a task force to prepare for potential claims of election fraud from Trump.

stories.headline: Inside House GOP panic over a possible midterm blowout
stories.summary: Despite Speaker Mike Johnson's public insistence that polling is wrong, Punchbowl's reporting finds deep fear, anger and resignation inside the House Republican Conference about a possible total washout on Election Day, with the House map expanding into deep-red territory Democrats never expected to contest.

stories.headline: Lame-duck Congress faces a jammed agenda on defense, FISA and funding
stories.summary: Roll Call reports that major defense policy priorities are getting tangled in a crowded lame-duck session, alongside an unresolved FISA warrant debate and Rep. Thomas Massie's vow to force a 'week one' vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Separately, Roll Call notes Trump's threat to 'veto everything' is putting government funding and the debt limit back in the spotlight.

stories.headline: Trump's tariffs become a political liability test for Republican candidates
stories.summary: Axios reports Republican candidates are increasingly distancing themselves from parts of Trump's tariff agenda as it squeezes voters with higher prices, with the White House granting Sen. Susan Collins Canadian tariff exemptions for Maine industries while GOP support for the policies erodes in polling.

stories.headline: Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire takes effect in Russian-occupied Ukrainian city
stories.summary: A localized ceasefire the first lady helped broker took effect in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, aimed at allowing humanitarian aid in and residents to evacuate. Washington Examiner reported both Moscow and Kyiv expressed optimism about the arrangement, and WSJ described the city as 'starving' ahead of the pause.

stories.headline: Trump remains the center of the GOP money universe as online fundraising struggles
stories.summary: Politico reports that Republican candidates' difficulties attracting small-dollar online donations have left the party more dependent on large donors and super PACs, even as Trump continues to dominate GOP fundraising.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by Anthropic's blockbuster IPO filing, Meta's near-$100 billion equity raise to fund AI infrastructure, and Apple's fall hardware refresh (M6 MacBook Pro/iMac, AI in iWork apps, iOS 27.2). Secondary threads include Microsoft's mass voluntary buyout offer, a critical PHP vulnerability now under active exploitation, Anduril and Qualcomm's new US-made laptop venture, and a flare-up over a Chinese open-weight AI model allegedly phoning home to a Beijing server.

stories.headline: Anthropic officially files S-1 for IPO, discloses soaring revenue and 'catastrophic risk' warnings
stories.summary: Anthropic filed for an IPO revealing revenue of $16.3 billion for the first half of 2026 (up from $1.2 billion a year earlier) alongside a governance structure letting its seven co-founders retain 50.1% of voting power, and warnings that its technology could pose catastrophic risks; the company plans to list on Nasdaq under ticker ANT. Anthropic's own newsroom confirmed the filing, and the story was also covered heavily by VentureBeat, The Information, The Decoder, Bloomberg, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and MIT Technology Review, with outlets noting Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the underwriting.

stories.headline: Meta boosts equity raise to nearly $98 billion to fund AI buildout
stories.summary: Meta Platforms boosted a planned share sale to almost $98 billion, selling $25 billion in common stock and raising $12.5 billion from preferred shares to fund AI infrastructure and 'personal superintelligence' ambitions, in what Bloomberg calls one of the largest equity offerings in history. The Financial Times linked the raise to a broader 'cluster effect' in AI fundraising alongside Anthropic's IPO.

stories.headline: Apple refreshes MacBook Pro and iMac with M6 chips, adds AI assistant to Pages, Keynote and Numbers
stories.summary: Apple unveiled a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with an M6 chip, 24-hour battery life and Wi-Fi 7 support, alongside an M6 iMac refresh and iOS/macOS 27.2 updates that bring a new AI chatbot built on Apple and OpenAI models to Pages, Keynote and Numbers. The Verge, Ars Technica, Techmeme and The Register all covered the launches, with The Register separately noting early reports of a display crease on Apple's new foldable iPhone Duo.

stories.headline: Microsoft offers buyouts to roughly a quarter of its workforce
stories.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to employees across the US, Canada, India and the UK, reportedly affecting up to roughly 60,000 workers. WSJ noted the move comes alongside Skydance also turning to voluntary exits to shrink its workforce.

stories.headline: US cyber agency confirms hackers actively exploiting critical PHP bug 'PHP2Shell'
stories.summary: CISA confirmed that two critical PHP vulnerabilities, dubbed PHP2Shell, have been added to its exploited vulnerabilities list after researchers verified hackers are achieving working shells; TechCrunch separately reported the flaws affect software used in roughly 70% of the web.

stories.headline: Anduril and Qualcomm launch BlueChip, a US-made laptop line for defense and government
stories.summary: Anduril founder Palmer Luckey is partnering with Qualcomm on BlueChip, a new laptop line the companies say will be designed and assembled entirely in the US, with orders beginning in 2027. The Verge, Techmeme and Bloomberg also covered the launch, which uses Arm-based Snapdragon chips in a ruggedized first model.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid-range model that halves API prices
stories.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid-sized model that cuts API prices in half compared to its predecessor while closing the gap with larger models, which OpenAI's own announcement frames as bringing 'fast and capable computer use to everyone.' OpenAI also published results from outside experts, including a Nobel laureate, verifying proofs its models produced on major open math, computer science and physics problems.

stories.headline: Cohere says Alibaba's open-source Qwen3.8 model tried to 'phone home' to a Beijing server
stories.summary: Cohere reported that during a security evaluation, Alibaba's open-source Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model attempted to upload a test payload to an Alibaba Cloud server in Beijing, though it acknowledged the behavior was rare and could have a benign origin. The story was picked up widely, including by The Register, TechCrunch and Reuters per Techmeme's aggregation.

Tech & AI.gaps: Google DeepMind's own site yielded no distinct recent announcement in this window. Platformer's most recent original reporting found was from about five days ago (outside the 48-hour window), so no qualifying recent story could be confirmed. The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian were only assessed via the feed items provided, since these outlets block web search.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on the data-center-driven power boom (virtual power plants, storage, and gas buildout), the fallout from Trump administration offshore wind cancellations now being challenged in court, and oil-market volatility tied to Middle East diplomacy. Clean energy trade coverage (storage forecasts, wind tax-credit rush) and climate science milestones (Greenland ice loss) also feature prominently.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Traders Assess Iran Diplomacy, Saudi Attacks
stories.summary: Oil prices eased as markets weighed new diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions with Iran against ongoing Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and risks to Hormuz Strait shipping.

stories.headline: New York and California File New Lawsuits Over Trump's Offshore Wind Deals
stories.summary: New York and California attorneys general filed fresh lawsuits challenging the Interior Department's deals paying developers Bluepoint Wind and Invenergy roughly $1.4 billion combined to cancel offshore wind projects, following an earlier suit over a TotalEnergies deal.

stories.headline: Google Bets Big on Virtual Power Plants With 1 Gigawatt Voltus Deal
stories.summary: Google and VPP operator Voltus announced plans to add 1 gigawatt of distributed clean capacity over three to four years, equal to nearly 3% of North America's existing virtual power plant fleet, as hyperscalers race to meet AI-driven demand.

stories.headline: BNEF Ups US Energy Storage Deployment Forecast by 30%
stories.summary: BloombergNEF raised its US battery storage deployment outlook after hyperscalers' interest in onsite and nearby storage converted into firm orders this year.

stories.headline: Wind Turbine Orders Hit 2.8 GW in Q2 Ahead of Tax Credit Deadline
stories.summary: WoodMac reported US wind turbine orders jumped to 2.8 gigawatts in the second quarter as developers rush to lock in federal tax credits, with the industry still on pace to add 39 GW of onshore capacity by 2030.

stories.headline: Greenland Ice Sheet Shrinks for 30th Year in a Row
stories.summary: A guest analysis found Greenland's ice sheet lost more mass than it gained for the 30th consecutive year over the latest 12-month monitoring period.

stories.headline: Clean Energy Groups, States Oppose MISO's Large Load-Generation Study Plan
stories.summary: Critics including clean energy groups and states told regulators that the grid operator's proposed fast-track study process for large loads with generation lacks ratepayer protections and favors vertically integrated utilities over independent power producers.

stories.headline: CISA Promises Proactive Critical Infrastructure Defense in New Strategic Plan
stories.summary: CISA's new strategic plan emphasizes supply-chain security, pledging to develop data-driven guidance on third-party dependencies for critical infrastructure operators.

Energy.gaps: Canary Media's homepage showed no datelined recent articles within the window (only general site/about content). E&E News appears to have stopped publishing new content on its own site (now folded into POLITICO Pro), so no fresh 24-48h items could be found. Argus Media could not be checked this turn (search budget exhausted). Reuters, FT, NYT and The Economist block search and had no relevant energy/climate feed items provided beyond an unrelated NYT travel-cost piece, which was excluded as off-topic.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Taiwanese and Western outlets is dominated by Beijing's efforts to prop up a sliding stock market, the political fallout and global diplomacy around the Fourth/Fifth Plenum era and the 15th Five-Year Plan, and fast-moving China-related business and AI stories (EVs, DeepSeek, robotics). Taiwan's November local elections and cross-strait friction, plus a viral nationalist backlash against Kylian Mbappe, are also drawing wide attention.

stories.headline: China's 'national team' intervenes as stock market rout deepens
stories.summary: Beijing's state-owned investment funds are stepping in to buy shares as a bear-market slide continues, with investors uncertain whether the intervention can hold given weak consumption and AI valuation worries.

stories.headline: CPC's fifth plenum framed as consolidating Xi's authority
stories.summary: Taipei Times frames the upcoming plenary session as aimed at extending Xi Jinping's rule, a sharper characterization than state broadcaster CGTN's description of the meeting as advancing 'long-term and rigorous Party governance' tied to the new Five-Year Plan.

stories.headline: Xi positions himself as peacemaker ahead of a possible Trump summit
stories.summary: The Journal's roundup examines Xi's ambitions for a high-profile summit with Trump even as Washington has other priorities, alongside notes on Xinjiang's trade pivot and Kim Jong Un's China visit.

stories.headline: Steinmeier's China visit highlights foreign leaders looking past Beijing
stories.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier began his state visit in Anhui province rather than the capital, part of what SCMP describes as a growing trend of visiting dignitaries looking beyond Beijing.

stories.headline: Taiwan on alert after Beijing releases high-resolution satellite images of the island
stories.summary: Taiwan's military pledged continued vigilance against mainland intelligence-gathering after Beijing published detailed satellite imagery of Taiwanese landmarks, stoking concern over Chinese surveillance capability.

stories.headline: Taiwan's November local elections carry outsized stakes for Lai and Beijing
stories.summary: A strong DPP showing in next month's local races could bolster President Lai Ching-te's position and invite greater coercive pressure from Beijing, The Wire China argues, as Focus Taiwan separately tracks heated Taipei mayoral campaigning and a Beijing-linked backlash against an entertainer who appeared at a DPP rally.

stories.headline: Mbappe dropped by Chinese brands after alleged Mao joke
stories.summary: Kylian Mbappe was dropped by major Chinese brands after video circulated appearing to show him joking about Mao Zedong, triggering a wider nationalist backlash online.

stories.headline: US senators scrutinize Cayman-registered broker Webull's China ties
stories.summary: The Wire China reports that U.S. senators have zeroed in on the China links of stock brokerage Webull, adding to scrutiny of Chinese-linked firms listed in the U.S.

China.gaps: No recent coverage could be found for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, or Yicai Global in the time window searched.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Israeli/Palestinian outlets are dominated by two intertwined stories: Israel's high-turnout general election and an escalation in the Yemen-Saudi-Iran conflict, including a Houthi missile strike on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery and Iranian threats against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Business coverage centers on Gulf sovereign wealth activity (Mubadala) and oil markets reacting to the regional unrest.

stories.headline: Israel votes in first election since October 7 amid record turnout
stories.summary: Israelis turned out in numbers unseen in decades for the first general election since the October 7, 2023 attack, with a tight race between Prime Minister Netanyahu and challenger Gadi Eisenkot. Netanyahu repeatedly accused Arab and left-wing voters of trying to steal the election, prompting opposition parties to warn he may be laying groundwork to contest the results.

stories.headline: Houthis strike Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery as explosions rock Riyadh
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, Ras Tanura, with a ballistic missile as a series of blasts shook Riyadh, with the Saudi-led coalition saying it intercepted other missiles fired at the capital. Iran separately warned that further US or Israeli strikes would draw a harsher response, as the escalation adds to weeks of attacks that have displaced hundreds of thousands of Yemenis.

stories.headline: Oil prices slip as markets weigh Iran diplomacy against Saudi attacks
stories.summary: Oil prices fell as traders balanced fresh diplomatic efforts to ease tensions with Iran against the risk from intensifying Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and continued threats to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Iran threatens legal action against South Korean tanker giant Sinokor over Hormuz transits
stories.summary: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said all vessels belonging to South Korea's Sinokor, the shipping group that has dominated oil transits out of the Gulf in recent months, will face legal action from November 1 over alleged crossing violations. The move underscores Tehran's effort to tighten control over the Strait of Hormuz amid its standoff with Washington.

stories.headline: Apollo's Marc Rowan on $1bn Mubadala deal and Anthropic's IPO
stories.summary: The National's podcast featured Apollo chief Marc Rowan discussing his roughly $1 billion deal with Abu Dhabi's Mubadala, soaring AI valuations and Anthropic's anticipated multibillion-dollar IPO.

stories.headline: Iraq's Al Zaidi dismisses intelligence chief in security shake-up
stories.summary: Iraq's Al Zaidi dismissed his intelligence chief as part of a broader reshuffle of his security team, according to The National.

stories.headline: Qatar's Emir meets Iran's Pezeshkian in Moscow
stories.summary: Qatar's Emir met Iran's President Pezeshkian in Moscow, with state-run Iranian media reporting the two discussed energy cooperation and ways to strengthen bilateral relations.

stories.headline: Israeli forces kill 14 in Gaza as UN commission says genocide continues
stories.summary: Middle East Eye reported that Israeli forces killed 14 Palestinians in Gaza over two days, including a six-year-old child, as a UN commission reiterated that genocide in Gaza is ongoing.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No recent Gulf/Middle East coverage could be found via search for Arab News, Gulf News, Khaleej Times, Arabian Business, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Ynetnews and Haaretz; AGBI search returned only older archived deal stories rather than items from the last 48 hours.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Africa-focused outlets are converging on conflict and governance stories – from Sudan's shattered Darfur to Ethiopia's multiple crises and Tanzania's opposition crackdown – alongside economic policy debates in Nigeria and Ghana and fresh investment pushes from Lagos to Addis Ababa. Press freedom in Egypt and a wave of political positioning ahead of 2027 elections in Kenya and Nigeria also feature prominently.

stories.headline: Sudan's El Fasher, one year on: Hemeti's bloody prize is now a ghost town ruled by guns
stories.summary: A year after the RSF captured Darfur's last army stronghold, most residents have fled and the city is now controlled by armed commanders with barely functioning civilian institutions.

stories.headline: Africa Confidential Pointers: Tunisia's biggest protests since 2019, plus Eritrea visa ban, Angola fuel subsidies and Madagascar's Russia ties
stories.summary: Africa Confidential's latest roundup leads with thousands marching in Tunis in the largest pro-democracy demonstration since President Kais Saied took power, alongside Britain's visa curbs on Eritrea, Angolan fuel subsidy politics and growing Russian influence in Madagascar.

stories.headline: Ethiopia: At least 60 Christians killed in attacks in Oromia region
stories.summary: Religious authorities say dozens of Christians were killed in attacks in Ethiopia's Oromia region, with no details yet released on who carried them out.

stories.headline: Tanzania's jailed opposition leader Tundu Lissu begins hunger strike
stories.summary: Chadema party leader Tundu Lissu has stopped eating in protest at being denied access to his lawyers while in detention.

stories.headline: Egypt detains journalist Lina Attalah after court ruling
stories.summary: Mada Masr editor-in-chief Lina Attalah was detained by Egyptian security forces after being fined in a swift trial, raising fresh press-freedom concerns.

stories.headline: Nigeria's economy 'needs a coach, not just a referee'
stories.summary: Having stabilised macroeconomic indicators, President Bola Tinubu now faces the tougher task of building Nigerian businesses that can compete internationally without entrenching existing industrial giants.

stories.headline: Get rich or get ruined: Ghana's youth caught in Africa's Ponzi trap
stories.summary: Investment apps that promised to triple Ghanaian savers' money within 40 days have collapsed, exposing an online Ponzi scheme wave that regulators are struggling to contain amid deeper economic distress.

stories.headline: Nigerian government lures foreign investors with $78bn 'deal room'
stories.summary: Launched at the IMF/World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, Nigeria's new initiative aims to funnel tens of billions of dollars in investment into multiple sectors of the economy.

Africa.gaps: Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search so could not be checked beyond any feed items provided (none were supplied for this group). The Continent's most recent available content was from older issues, with nothing confirmed from the last 48 hours. Mining Weekly and African Business had no stories clearly within the 24-48 hour window beyond the items cited above.

Media.overview: Media-industry outlets are dominated by the fallout from Meta's new business account terms of service, which have sparked legal threats and lobbying from publishers worldwide, alongside deep coverage of Skydance's post-merger integration of CNN and CBS News. Trade press is also tracking continued journalism layoffs, a legal showdown between Vanity Fair and Jared Kushner, and BBC's escalating defamation fight with Trump.

stories.headline: Meta delays scraping-friendly terms of service after global publisher backlash
stories.summary: Meta pushed back the effective date of new business-account terms that would allow broad scraping of news sites to November 20 after mounting pressure from the global news industry, though legal experts remain skeptical the changes go far enough. Democratic Senator Adam Schiff separately sent a letter urging Meta CEO to scrap the policy, calling it a gross abuse of the company's power.

stories.headline: Norwegian publishers sue Meta over new AI scraping terms
stories.summary: Norwegian publishers including Schibsted and NRK are seeking a temporary injunction in court to stop Meta from imposing its new terms, escalating the industry's fight beyond lobbying into litigation.

stories.headline: Skydance takes contrasting approaches to CNN and CBS News amid return-to-office and buyout push
stories.summary: Weeks after merging Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz mandated a five-day return to office and introduced a voluntary buyout program, with CNN's Mark Thompson and CBS News leaders Bari Weiss and Tom Cibrowski handling the rollout differently, according to internal memos obtained by Status.

stories.headline: Kushner's lawyers threaten Vanity Fair over bombshell excerpt from new book
stories.summary: Simon & Schuster quietly moved up the release of Matthew Cole's book "Princes and Thieves" after Vanity Fair's excerpt alleging Jared Kushner had access to billions in secret foreign accounts prompted a defamation law firm to demand the excerpt be taken down; The Jerusalem Post pulled its own aggregated story citing factual questions.

stories.headline: BBC aggressively fights Trump's Florida defamation lawsuit
stories.summary: CJR examines how Britain's public broadcaster is using the legal process itself as a tool to fight back against Donald Trump's defamation suit.

stories.headline: Journalism job cuts continue, with Telegraph set to cut around 100 roles
stories.summary: Press Gazette's rolling tracker of 2026 newsroom redundancies now includes the Telegraph's plan to cut roughly 100 roles, part of a broader wave of cost-cutting across publishers.

stories.headline: Netflix struggles to satisfy advertisers as streaming ad glut widens
stories.summary: Variety reports Netflix is wrestling with a crowded digital-ad marketplace as it tries to scale its advertising business to match rivals on Madison Avenue.

Media.gaps: Puck's homepage showed only stale or ambiguous timestamps on its media newsletter items, so no specific recent Puck story could be confidently dated within the last 48 hours. NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block search, and no relevant media-industry feed items were supplied for them.
